name: Geese
label: Partisan Records
lede: Five kids from Brooklyn Friends School started with a Tame Impala cover in a Fort Greene basement and ended up with the best-reviewed rock record of 2025.

eras.title: Rock school, then the basement
eras.text: Geese begin as schoolmates in Brooklyn who practice in a Fort Greene basement and put out two self-released records they later pull from streaming. The band nearly ends when college looms.

years.cap: Cameron Winter, frontman of the band Geese performing at The Stage at Suffolk Downs in Boston as the openers for... · Wikimedia
years.h: A Tame Impala cover in Max Bassin's basement
years.p: Cameron Winter, Emily Green, Dominic DiGesu and Max Bassin meet at Brooklyn Friends School and the Park Slope Rock School. Their first song together is Tame Impala's "Mind Mischief".
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band practiced and recorded in Bassin's Fort Greene basement. The name comes from Green's childhood nickname, Goose.

years.h: Two self-released records, both later pulled
years.p: An untitled EP arrives April 21, 2018, then the album A Beautiful Memory on July 13. Both have since been removed from streaming.

years.h: Bottomless Pink Lagoon EP, with Foster Hudson on guitar
years.p: Hudson joins as a second guitarist in 2019, and the band self-releases the EP on August 18. He stays through 2023.

eras.title: Signed before they graduate
eras.text: A manager finds a SoundCloud upload, a label bets on a teenage band, and the debut arrives with a sound that turns heads.

years.src: Wikipedia: Emily Green · Wikipedia: Projector · Wikipedia: Cameron Winter
years.h: Willie Upbin finds them and Partisan signs them
years.p: The band nearly breaks up for college until manager Willie Upbin scouts them in 2020, then they sign to Partisan Records. Winter skips Boston University to keep going.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Projector page says the record was first uploaded to SoundCloud, where Upbin found it and pitched it around. It says the band picked Partisan because they saw it as "the best of the worst" among labels.

q: It was this transcendental moment where we were all really in the zone.
years.p: Recorded in Bassin's basement studio, "the Nest", late 2019 into early 2020, mixed by Dan Carey. Pitchfork gave it 6.6.
years.xp: Metacritic lists 83 from eight reviews; NME called it one of the year's most thrilling rock debuts. Winter told Apple Music 1's Matt Wilkinson about the session where it clicked.

eras.title: Jam band, sort of
eras.text: With Sam Revaz on keys and James Ford producing, Geese loosen up and get strange, and then lose a guitarist.

years.h: 3D Country turns post-punk into a proud jam band
years.p: James Ford produces at the Diamond Mine in Queens. Pitchfork's Brady Gerber gives it 6.8 and hears a band with newfound dynamics and space.
years.xp: An EP, 4D Country, follows on October 13 with four more tracks from the same sessions. Metacritic shows 78 from six reviews.

years.h: Foster Hudson leaves to focus on school
years.p: Hudson departs after 3D Country, and Geese continue as a four-piece with Sam Revaz touring on keys.

eras.title: Winter goes solo, Geese go live
eras.text: A live album, a run of opening slots and a solo record from the frontman widen the audience before the next Geese album.

years.h: Alive & in Person gets the room on tape
years.p: A live album on Partisan, released as Geese open for Greta Van Fleet and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Green came out publicly through the release. Green also has a side project, Star's Revenge, with Sunflower Bean drummer Olive Faber.

years.p: A record of piano and baritone that drags his name well beyond Geese. Pitchfork ranked it No. 3 of 2025 and named "Love Takes Miles" the best song.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports Nick Cave called Winter's vocals "glorious" and that the New York Times' Lizzy Goodman described it as received as a tour de force.

eras.title: Getting Killed
eras.text: Ten days in Los Angeles, Kenny Beats in the room, and a record that critics pile onto.

years.h: Ten days at Putnam Hill while Los Angeles burns
years.p: Geese record with Kenny Beats, roughly fourteen hours a day, as wildfires hit Southern California.
years.xp: Wikipedia's page on "Taxes" reports the band co-produced with Kenny Beats, working about fourteen hours daily over ten days at Putnam Hill.

years.h: "Taxes" ends in a mosh pit that eats itself
years.p: The lead single arrives with Noel Paul's video, which goes from live footage to cannibal chaos. Geese play it on Jimmy Kimmel Live! from Brooklyn on October 1.
years.xp: NME and Stereogum both ranked the song No. 2 for 2025, Pitchfork No. 10, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Getting Killed · Wikipedia: Cameron Winter
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 9.0 and Best New Music, then ranked it No. 7 of 2025. Reviewer Sam Sodomsky called it their strangest and strongest work.
years.xp:
Metacritic lists 89. Stereogum, NME and the New Yorker all put it first; Rolling Stone had it fifth. It reached No. 96 on the Billboard 200 and No. 26 in the UK.

Two records earlier, Pitchfork had given the band 6.6 and then 6.8.

years.cap: Dominic DiGesu, bassist of the band Geese performing at The Stage at Suffolk Downs in Boston as the openers for King... · Wikimedia
years.h: Winter headlines Carnegie Hall, and Paul Thomas Anderson films it
years.p: Wikipedia calls him one of the youngest artists to play the room; Benny Safdie assisted on the shoot.
They play "Au Pays du Cocaine" and "Trinidad".
years.xp: Billboard and Rolling Stone covered the debut.

years.h: BBC's Sound of 2026 puts them fourth; the Brits give them a trophy
years.p: Geese win International Group of the Year at the 2026 Brit Awards, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Wired ties their PR firm to fake-account campaigns
years.p: Wired reported that Chaotic Good Projects ran campaigns for Winter and Geese. Co-founder Adam Tarsia confirmed the firm engineered them.
years.xp: Musician Eliza McLamb, whose Substack post prompted the story, said she does not consider Geese a "psy-op". Other writers argued the tactics are common.
